output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely a floors 6-8 problem caused by the CH-2 chiller failure from 4 to 19 August. Floors 6-8 fell from 8.6 to 7.4 overall, with room comfort at 6.1, while floors 1-5 moved only 0.1, within normal variation. Heat complaints (56 of 61 floors 6-8 negatives) and recorded room temperatures of 26.5-29 C match the outage window, and scores recovered after the repair. The housekeeping contractor is not the explanation: cleanliness held steady and inspection pass rates were flat. The kiosks are not the explanation either: check-in scores were unchanged. The rate rise is a weak explanation; the value dip is similar to last year's seasonal pattern, and the overall score barely moved on floors 1-5. I am fairly confident about the chiller cause, less so about the size of the rate effect. Next steps: reinstate the deferred maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spare parts, and write a cooling-outage recovery protocol. Do not serve notice on Orrin, do not pull the kiosks, and do not drop the floors 6-8 responses from the score. Confirming the cause would need engineering records, which I did not collect.
